## UnreachableError class

Thrown when control reaches a branch that the static types say cannot be reached, for example the `default` case of an exhaustive `switch` over a closed enum.

**Signature:**

```typescript
declare class UnreachableError extends Error
```

**Extends:** Error

## Remarks

The constructor accepts only `never`<!-- -->. Passing the switched-on value in a `default` branch therefore compiles only while every member is handled, so adding a member turns each unhandled switch into a compile error. At runtime (for example after an unchecked cast), the error reports the unexpected value so the failure is actionable.

This is a caller-side programming error, not an operation outcome. It is not part of the structured error family and never crosses the wire.

## Example

```ts
switch (status) {
  case 'confirmed':
  case 'tentative':
    return true
  case 'cancelled':
    return false
  default:
    throw new UnreachableError(status, 'event status')
}
```
